title: A Feather Duster Became a Mom for Two Orphaned Baby Turkeys!
summary: Imagine you're a baby turkey, just a day old, and suddenly you're all alone. That's what happened to two little turkey chicks in Pennsylvania. Their mom and a sibling were killed on a road, and the chicks were found running scared. They needed warmth and comfort, fast. At the Raven Ridge Wildlife Center, the staff had a surprising idea: they hung a feather duster inside a warm incubator. Why? Because to a baby turkey, a fluffy feather duster feels a lot like a mother turkey's feathers! The chicks could hide under it, just like they would with their real mom. Tracie Young, the center's director, said it helped them feel safe and less stressed. They even put up pictures of adult turkeys so the chicks could see what they should grow up to be. This isn't the first time the center used a feather duster—they've done it before, and it always helps. The chicks started eating more and gaining weight. They'll stay at the center until fall, when they're big enough to live in the wild. It's a simple trick, but it shows how a little creativity can save scared, orphaned animals.
why_it_matters: This story shows that even simple ideas can help save helpless animals, teaching us that we can all find clever ways to care for living things in trouble.

Wildlife centers like Raven Ridge (a Pennsylvania animal rescue) often raise orphaned chicks using special tricks.
Turkeys are native to North America and were once almost extinct but have made a comeback.
